answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a staked identity anchor: each participant locks a bond bound to one non-transferable human attestation, and only that anchor confers voting weight. Reputation accrues slowly, so a fresh cluster of fake agents carries little more than a whisper. To impersonate many agents, an attacker must buy a distinct real attestation and post a bond for every Sybil, so cost rises linearly with each forged identity. Reused anchors get slashed, turning the fable of free identities into a losing trade.
